transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-22
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 51 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Priya (SolaceBridge Head of Platform), Marcus (CTO), Evan (SRE), Nora (FinOps)
Shared artifacts: Slides: https://redwood.ai/decks/solacebridge-console-walkthrough, Pilot template: https://redwood.ai/pilots/solacebridge, Perf benchmark sheet (snippet) shared in chat

Summary (auto): quick console walkthrough focused on per-route telemetry, usage velocity, cost breakdown and pilot scope. Customer primarily interested in mapping routes to chargeback units and reducing tail latency for interactive product features. Security and data residency questions raised.

Topics: Console overview; Per-route dashboards; Token-level costing and SLI/SLO correlation; Batching / caching recommendations; Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs; Pilot scope and next steps

Action items (auto): see Action Items field

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick intros — i m Maya, account exec, Liam and Ravi are with me on the engineering side. how's everyone doing over at SolaceBridge?
[00:22] Priya (SolaceBridge): Good, thanks. busy quarter but excited to see the console. Nora from FinOps will be listening in for cost questions.
[00:30] Marcus (SolaceBridge): hey, Marcus. we run a multi-tenant platform for customer messaging, latency matters for the live channels. we're curious about mapping our feature routes to cost buckets.
[00:45] Liam (Redwood): great — that's exactly what we'll focus on. quick agenda: show per-route telemetry, then cost breakdowns, then routing/fallbacks and finally pilot scoping. sound ok?
[01:12] Evan (SolaceBridge): sounds good. FYI our stack is GKE + internal envoy + tokenization on the app side. we currently call two vendors for generation, looking to reduce costs and standardize.
[01:35] Ravi (Redwood): perfect, can you share approximate volume numbers and percentiles? even ballpark helps us suggest configs.
[01:40] Evan: sure, peak qps for the real-time channel is ~600 rps, p95 latency target is 200 ms, average prompt length around 180 tokens.
[02:01] Maya: quick clarification — when you say "routes" do you map by endpoint (e.g., /api/generate/chat) or by user-facing feature?
[02:12] Priya: by feature — we have 'live-typing', 'summarize-thread', and 'safety-rerank' as primary features. each has different latency and cost sensitivity.
[02:30] Liam: ok walking into the console now — on screen you can see the routes list, we surface route-level QPS, token consumption, and an inferred cost per route over the chosen billing window.
[02:58] [screen share starts — console UI noise, mouse clicks]
[03:10] Liam: here's 'live-typing' route, notice the token mix graph, region split, and importantly the latency vs cost scatter where we bucket requests by model variant and sequence length.
[03:32] Marcus: that latency vs cost scatter is helpful. does the console estimate on-prem cost if we run private?
[03:40] Liam: we show a normalized cost estimate for hosted vs dedicated vs private (estimated infra compute only) — it's a model, not a bill. for private we need your hw profile to tighten estimates.
[04:05] Priya: can we tag routes with business units? we need to charge product teams monthly.
[04:15] Maya: yes tags are first-class — you can map routes to labels and export a CSV for chargeback. Nora, that should help finance reconcile.
[04:30] Nora (SolaceBridge): that helps. can we see an example export?
[04:36] Liam: sure — exporting now. the CSV contains route id, label, token counts, estimated cost, p50/p95 latencies.
[04:50] [file export sound]
[05:02] Liam: also note the per-token breakdown — we show model, decode tokens, and prefix cache hits. prefix cache shows up as 'KV cache' sometimes in logs, we try to highlight cache hit rate — higher hit rate reduces per-request cost by avoiding decode.
[05:27] Evan: small nit — in our infra we already maintain a prefix cache service, would Redwood cache layer conflict?
[05:40] Ravi: not necessarily, we can integrate with your cache via the routing layer or turn our automatic prefix caching off. there s a config flag for 'external cache' mode.
[05:58] Priya: can you walk through an example where we reduce cost by changing batching or model variant?
[06:10] Liam: yep — here's a real customer case: 'summarize-thread' was using base-8 model at 2x tokens, we suggested switching to a distilled variant and enabling batching; cost dropped 38% while p95 stayed within SLA because queries aggregated into 20–40ms extra queuing but decode saved huge compute.
[06:45] Marcus: what's the default batching timeout? we can t add noticeable latency for live-typing.
[06:52] Liam: default is dynamic — it adapts by route to keep tail latency within configured SLO. you can set max_wait_ms per route, so for live-typing you'd set max_wait_ms=5–15 and batching won't add real user-visible latency.
[07:12] [brief cross-talk — customer asking about SDKs]
[07:30] Maya: also want to touch on routing policies — you can set a cost-first or latency-first policy per route, with fallback to cheaper model variants if capacity is low.
[07:50] Priya: we have compliance needs — do you have SOC2, SAML? what about KMS for keys?
[07:58] Liam: yes SOC2 Type II, we support SAML SSO and RBAC, and for private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM. i ll share the security pack after the call.
[08:20] Marcus: any audit log details? we need token-level logging for ATO reviews.
[08:28] Ravi: we provide audit logs with per-request metadata (route id, model version, tokens used), and for hosted we redact customer content unless you opt in to store raw inputs — private deploy keeps everything on your infra.
[08:50] Priya: ok good. back to console — how do we detect regressions if a model update drops quality?
[08:58] Liam: we integrate with Redwood Optimize for evaluations. you can tie prompt sets to routes and get quality diff alerts; we also support canary rollouts (5/20/100) with automatic fallback if quality or latency regresses.
[09:22] Evan: useful. can we run a smoke test with our sample traffic?
[09:27] Ravi: yes in the pilot we'll run a short benchmark using your sample prompts and measure cost/latency — we can share the raw CSV and dashboard.
[09:45] [screen scroll to per-route traces]
[09:55] Liam: here is a trace view for a single 'live-typing' request — shows middleware times, tokenization, model decode time, and routing decision (hosted vs dedicated). you can drill to logs and see percentiles across time windows.
[10:20] Priya: those middleware times are great for pinpointing where tail latency comes from.
[10:30] Marcus: about chargeback — how does the console treat system tokens like reranks or internal ops? we need to exclude internal housekeeping requests.
[10:40] Liam: we let you set tag filters and ignore patterns (e.g., route.name startsWith 'internal_') so exports only include billable routes.
[10:53] Nora: is there an integration to our billing system? we run NetSuite — ideally automated ingestion.
[10:59] Maya: we have a billing export API and S3 drop; customers have built automated ETL to NetSuite or Snowflake using route-level exports.
[11:15] [pause — chat links posted: security pack, pricing snippet]
[11:25] Priya: curious about regional routing — some traffic must stay in eu-west due to residency. can console route by region?
[11:33] Ravi: yes you can pin routes to allowed regions and set fallbacks only within the same residency scope. we also surface per-region cost deltas so you can see how running in eu-west affects unit cost.
[11:52] Evan: performance question — do you pre-warm KV cache for hotspot users? we see bursts from certain accounts.
[12:02] Liam: yes warmup policies exist — you can tag VIP tenants and pre-warm KV entries or reserve dedicated capacity for them.
[12:18] [transition to cost modeling]
[12:25] Liam: switching to the cost-breakdown panel — we show cost per token, per model, decode vs encode split, and an allocation engine that maps requests to business unit shares.
[12:40] Marcus: can we see a hypothetical month where 60% traffic is live-typing and 40% summary?
[12:47] Liam: yep — using the 'Scenario builder' you can inject traffic mix, change model choices, toggle caching, and see projected spend and latency SLO impacts.
[13:05] [Liam creates scenario live — fiddling noises]
[13:18] Priya: I like the scenario builder. can we export multiple scenarios to compare?
[13:22] Liam: export as JSON or CSV, good for finance reviews.
[13:30] Nora: do you support per-route budget alerts?
[13:35] Maya: yes threshold alerts (percent of budget, spend growth rate) go to Slack/email and can open a ticket in your PagerDuty.
[13:50] Evan: on the models — you mentioned Redwood-verified model variants. do you host open models or proprietary ones?
[13:58] Liam: we host a curated catalog of open models and also run private customer models for private deployments. for compliance-sensitive features you can bring-your-own-model (BYOM) and pin the version.
[14:18] Marcus: what's the SLA for dedicated pools?
[14:23] Ravi: dedicated has SLA commitments for throughput and availability — we can share baseline numbers in the proposal.
[14:32] [short break in conversation while customers check slides]
[15:00] Priya: this is great — can you show the anomaly detection that flagged weird token spikes? last month we had a burst and it cost us.
[15:10] Liam: sure — anomaly detection uses route baselines and flags unusual increases in tokens, latency, or model shifts; alerts include suggested mitigations like reducing max_seq or switching model variant.
[15:30] Marcus: can the system auto-roll back an offending rollout?
[15:36] Ravi: yes if you enable automatic fallback policy a canary that trips quality or cost limits can be rolled back to the previous variant automatically.
[15:50] Priya: about pilot scope — what does a standard pilot include?
[15:58] Maya: standard pilot is 2–4 weeks: initial discovery, sample data run (benchmarks), a sandbox of the console with route-level telemetry, and a short ops handoff. pilot pricing is typically credit-based; we'll include expected infra cost estimate in the proposal.
[16:20] Nora: will we be able to run the pilot in our VPC?
[16:26] Ravi: yes for private pilots we can deploy a cloud-connector into your VPC; for hosted pilots we collect telemetry via a minimal agent — we ll recommend private if data residency or PII is involved.
[16:45] Evan: one more technical — how do you handle KV cache persistence across restarts? we need to maintain warm cache on pod rotation.
[16:55] Liam: KV cache can be backed by local NVMe with snapshotting or an external Redis cluster — for mission-critical flows we recommend persistent backing with pre-warm hooks.
[17:10] [customer asks a deep-dive about token accounting]
[17:18] Liam: token accounting: we attribute tokens to route with rules; system tokens can be assigned to a 'platform' bucket. decode tokens get counted heavier in cost model because of GPU cycles. we surface per-token unit cost and cumulative spend by route.
[17:45] Marcus: do you show cost per 1000 requests as well as per-token?
[17:53] Liam: yes both metrics available — per-req, per-1k, and per-token, and you can aggregate by label or team.
[18:05] Priya: how about retention windows for metrics? we need 12 months for audits.
[18:12] Ravi: console stores detailed telemetry for 90 days in the standard tier; extended retention (12–36 months) is an add-on — logs and aggregated metrics can be exported to S3 for long term storage.
[18:30] [short silence, participants typing in chat]
[18:50] Liam: quick demo of a drill — opening a route that spiked last week. you can see a correlation view: traffic spike aligns with a model rollout and a third-party downstream delay.
[19:05] Priya: nice correlation, would help our incident reviews.
[19:12] Mara — small mis-said (speaker mis tag)
[19:20] Maya: ok let s talk timeline — what needs to happen for a pilot next week?
[19:28] Marcus: we need internal approval, procurement will want the security docs, and FinOps will want an initial forecast.
[19:40] Maya: we will send a one-pager with estimated monthly cost under three scenarios (hosted, dedicated reserve, private) and pilot terms.
[19:50] Nora: who will own the pricing model?
[19:54] Maya: I will — Maya will draft the pilot pricing and expected credits, include sample scenario numbers.
[20:05] Evan: technical onboarding — who runs the benchmark?
[20:10] Ravi: our SE team will run it with your sample prompts; we'll ask for a 2-hour window to stream traffic at safe QPS for the benchmark.
[20:22] [transition — Liam shows Optimize integration briefly]
[20:30] Liam: Optimize suggests quantization and batching profiles by route; here it recommends INT8 for non-latency-critical summarize-thread route and a quantization profile that saves ~27% compute.
[20:50] Marcus: any quality degradation risk?
[20:54] Liam: Optimize runs evals against your golden prompt set and reports delta; quantization is only suggested if quality drop is within acceptable bounds (configurable).
[21:10] Priya: ok let's close with recap and owners.
[21:16] Maya: recap — Redwood to send: pilot proposal + pricing (Maya) by 4/24, security pack + SOC2 evidence (Liam) by 4/23, recorded console video + scenario exports (Ravi) by 4/23. SolaceBridge to send: sample routes and prompt sets (Evan) by 4/26, internal decision maker list for procurement (Priya) by 4/25.
[21:46] Marcus: timeline seems fair. one ask — can you include expected SLA numbers in the pilot doc?
[21:52] Ravi: yes will include baseline SLA and dedicated pool options.
[22:00] [closing pleasantries]
[22:10] Maya: thanks everyone, we ll follow up with invites for the pilot kickoff.
[22:18] Priya: thanks, appreciated.
[22:22] [call ends — recording stops]

Notes on transcription: some speaker labels were auto-assigned, occasional homophones (KV cash) and product shorthand (Redwood Optics instead of Redwood Optimize) present in the transcription.

Recap (auto): Pilot approved pending security review and pricing. Key interests: mapping routes to cost centers, preserving p95 latency for 'live-typing', and running a 2–4 week pilot to measure cost/latency tradeoffs.
